origin: A concept from prospect theory, published by Daniel Kahneman and Amos Tversky in 1979.
whenToUse: You set the tone of benefit wording.
You report real losses, such as a warning that unsaved work will be lost.
You compare the same information told two ways.
whenNotToUse: You'd say a benefit that won't disappear is disappearing.
You'd push sign-ups with the pressure that declining is a loss.
You'd use warning colors when nothing is really lost.
accessibility: Use warning-like colors and icons only when there's real risk.
State the benefit's conditions (period, amount) clearly in words.
Show the options at the same size and weight.
